---
title: "Fit multiple fisheries and surveys"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE),
    file.path(guide_root, "NAMESPACE"))
} else {
  c(list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"),
    pattern = "[.](R|rdb|rdx)$", full.names = TRUE),
    system.file("NAMESPACE", package = "tinyAM"))
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", warning = TRUE,
  cache.extra = list(package = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
    R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
    mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")),
    sources = unname(tools::md5sum(source_files)),
    inputs = sim_cod_obs, truth = sim_cod_truth))
```

Different fishing gears remove different parts of a shared population. When
the fleet mix changes, the age pattern of total fishing mortality can change
too. This guide compares a fit to individual fleet catches with a fit to their
sum. Both fits use the same survey indices and population biology.

The simulated cod stock declines over 20 years. Trawl fishing drops to a low
bycatch level from year 11, while gillnet and longline fishing continue. Two survey
programs represent an offshore research-vessel survey and a coastal Sentinel
gillnet survey. The example uses [SimSurvey](https://paulregular.github.io/SimSurvey/).
The [dataset help](../reference/sim_cod_obs.html) describes the 3Ps cod
inspiration, simulation and generating values.

## Inspect the input keys

```{r inputs}
dat <- sim_cod_obs
check_tam_data(dat)
head(dat$catch)
head(dat$index)
```

Catch has a complete year–age grid within each `fleet`, with `NA` for
unavailable observations. Each index row identifies `survey` and `samp_time`.
Both surveys sample at the start of each year (`samp_time = 0`).

The Sentinel-like survey samples a coastal band more densely than the RV-like
survey samples offshore. Its dome-shaped selection contrasts with ascending
RV selection. Both use swept-area sampling, so the Sentinel-like program
approximates the footprint and selectivity of a gillnet survey.

```{r footprints, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap="Survey footprints on the synthetic grid. The northern edge represents the coast; grey cells are outside each survey's footprint."}
local({
  old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.8, 2.2, 0.8),
             mgp = c(2.8, 0.8, 0), cex = 0.85)
  on.exit(par(old))
  grid <- sim_cod_truth$footprint
  for (survey in c("RV", "Sentinel")) {
    selected <- grid[[survey]]
    plot(grid$x, grid$y, asp = 1, pch = 15, cex = 0.45,
      col = "grey90", xlab = "East-west (km)", ylab = "North-south (km)",
      main = if (survey == "RV") "RV-like" else "Sentinel-gillnet-like")
    points(grid$x[selected], grid$y[selected], pch = 15, cex = 0.45,
      col = tam_cols()[if (survey == "RV") 1 else 7])
  }
})
```

SimSurvey's `run_catch()` uses sampled fish ages and reported annual fleet totals
to estimate catch at age. It also estimates catch weights, using stock weight
in the tinyAM inputs where a fleet has no estimate. The fit takes stock
weights and maturity from the simulated population. `run_strat()` estimates
abundance within each survey's footprint. The input tables retain zero
estimates, which the lognormal likelihood excludes.
The simulation uses a fixed spatial pattern on a 20-by-20 grid, so the share
of the population available to each survey is approximately constant.

## See how fishing changes

Each fleet's reference F at full selectivity follows its own log-scale random
walk. From year 11, the trawl rate is 20% of what its random walk would
otherwise produce. Gillnet and longline follow their own paths through the
change.

```{r fishing-scenario, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Fleet targets at full selectivity. The vertical line marks the trawl reduction between years 10 and 11."}
local({
  targets <- sim_cod_truth$fishery_annual
  paths <- split(targets, targets$fishery)
  colors <- tam_pal(length(paths))
  max_F <- max(unlist(lapply(paths, `[[`, "F_full_reference"))) * 1.05
  plot(range(targets$year), c(0, max_F), type = "n",
    xlab = "Year", ylab = "Fully selected F target (per year)")
  abline(v = 10.5, lty = 3)
  for (i in seq_along(paths)) {
    d <- paths[[i]]
    lines(d$year, d$F_full_reference, col = colors[i], lwd = 2)
  }
  legend("bottomleft", legend = names(paths), col = colors, lty = 1, lwd = 2, bty = "n")
})

annual_fbar <- function(year, rate, abundance) {
  totals <- aggregate(cbind(FN = rate * abundance, N = abundance), list(year = year), sum)
  data.frame(year = totals$year, F = totals$FN / totals$N)
}
trawl_fbar <- with(subset(sim_cod_truth$fleet, fleet == "Trawl" & age %in% 5:10),
  annual_fbar(year, F_realized, N))
trawl_before <- mean(trawl_fbar$F[trawl_fbar$year <= 10])
trawl_after <- mean(trawl_fbar$F[trawl_fbar$year >= 11])
m_by_period <- with(sim_cod_truth$checks$realized_M_by_period, setNames(mean, period))
```

Realized F also depends on which ages the fleets catch. The trawl's average
realized F over ages 5–10 falls from `r sprintf("%.3f", trawl_before)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", trawl_after)` per year between the two periods. The simulation
draws reference M independently of the fishing targets. Realized M is the part
of Z that remains after accounting for actual fleet catches.
Recruitment also varies substantially through the decline.

## Describe each fleet within one formula

`for_fleet()` gives each fleet its own scale and curve. Inner formulas include
intercepts, so use outer `~ 0 +` to avoid an extra common baseline.

```{r fleet-formula, cache=TRUE}
fleet_dat <- dat
fleet_dat$catch <- transform(dat$catch, trawl_low = year >= 11)
fishing <- ~ 0 +
  for_fleet("Trawl", ~ logistic(age) + trawl_low) +
  for_fleet("Longline", ~ logistic(age)) +
  for_fleet("Gillnet", ~ double_logistic(age))
```

Trawl and longline selectivity rise with age. Gillnet selectivity is
dome-shaped. The `trawl_low` term lets the trawl scale shift in year 11 while
keeping its selectivity curve. The fit estimates the size of the shift.

```{r selection, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap="Generating selectivity curves. Dashed lines identify surveys; solid lines identify fisheries."}
local({
  curves <- sim_cod_truth$selectivity
  components <- c("Trawl", "Longline", "Gillnet", "RV", "Sentinel")
  colors <- tam_cols()[c(1, 2, 3, 6, 7)]
  line_types <- c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2)
  plot(range(curves$age), c(0, 1), type = "n",
    xlab = "Age (years)", ylab = "Selectivity")
  for (i in seq_along(components)) {
    d <- curves[curves$component == components[i], ]
    lines(d$age, d$selectivity, col = colors[i], lty = line_types[i], lwd = 2)
  }
  legend("bottomright", legend = components, col = colors, lty = line_types,
    lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
})
```

The double-logistic curve can peak below one, so its peak mean F can be lower
than its scale parameter. See [fleet formulas](../reference/for_fleet.html)
and [double-logistic curves](../reference/double_logistic.html).

## Give surveys their own relationships

```{r survey-formula, cache=TRUE}
catchability <- ~ 0 +
  for_survey("RV", ~ logistic(age)) +
  for_survey("Sentinel", ~ age + I(age ^ 2))
```

Each survey has a separate q scale and shape. A quadratic in age can
describe a dome on the log q scale with fewer parameters than a double-logistic
curve. This helps when few Sentinel observations are positive at the youngest
and oldest ages. Here q also includes the fraction of the population inside
the survey footprint.

## Fit the fleet and aggregate models

Use deterministic cohort survival, random-walk recruitment and M fixed at
0.3 per year in both models. Realized M over ages 5–10 averages
`r sprintf("%.3f", m_by_period[["Before"]])` before and
`r sprintf("%.3f", m_by_period[["After"]])` after the trawl reduction.
Fitting `ages = 1:14` pools catches and survey indices from ages 14–20
while retaining age-specific weights and maturity for biomass and SSB.

```{r multifleet, cache=TRUE, dependson=c("fleet-formula", "survey-formula"), results='hide'}
multifleet <- fit_tam(
  fleet_dat, ages = 1:14,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = fishing,
                    sd_form = ~ 1, mean_ages = 5:10),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3), mean_ages = 5:10),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 0 + fleet),
  index_settings = list(q_form = catchability, sd_form = ~ 0 + survey)
)
```

The fleet model estimates independent F deviations around each fleet's age
curve. It shares one process SD and one catch observation SD across fleets
because separate SDs were poorly identified in this example. Each fleet's
Baranov catch prediction uses its own F and the common total mortality
$Z = M + \sum_f F_f$.

For the aggregate model, sum catches across fleets at each year and age
before forming the plus group. A missing fleet catch makes the sum missing.
Compute a catch-number-weighted weight at age so the pooled data give the
same observed yield before plus-group pooling. Use the stock weight where
total catch is zero or missing.

```{r aggregate-inputs, cache=TRUE}
stock_weight <- subset(dat$weight, type == "stock")
fleet_weights <- subset(dat$weight, type == "catch", select = c(year, age, fleet, obs))
names(fleet_weights)[names(fleet_weights) == "obs"] <- "weight"
fleet_catch <- merge(dat$catch, fleet_weights, by = c("year", "age", "fleet"))
fleet_catch$yield <- fleet_catch$obs * fleet_catch$weight
totals <- aggregate(fleet_catch[c("obs", "yield")], fleet_catch[c("year", "age")], sum)

aggregate_dat <- dat
aggregate_dat$catch <- transform(totals[c("year", "age", "obs")],
  unit = unique(dat$catch$unit))
pooled_weight <- merge(totals, stock_weight[c("year", "age", "obs", "unit")],
  by = c("year", "age"), suffixes = c("", "_stock"))
pooled_weight <- transform(pooled_weight,
  obs = ifelse(!is.na(obs) & obs > 0, yield / obs, obs_stock),
  type = "catch", fleet = NA_character_)
aggregate_dat$weight <- rbind(stock_weight, pooled_weight[names(stock_weight)])
```

The aggregate model uses an AR1 process around age-specific mean F.
Departures from the mean are correlated across years and neighboring ages.
The model learns the timing of changes from the pooled catches and survey
indices.

```{r aggregate-fit, cache=TRUE, dependson=c("aggregate-inputs", "survey-formula"), results='hide'}
aggregate_fit <- fit_tam(
  aggregate_dat, ages = 1:14,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = ~ logistic(age), mean_ages = 5:10),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3), mean_ages = 5:10),
  index_settings = list(q_form = catchability, sd_form = ~ 0 + survey)
)
```

```{r checks}
check_tam(multifleet, aggregate_fit)
```

The fitted plus group applies its modeled mortality rates to ages 14 and
older. The generator drops surviving age-20 fish at the next year boundary.
These survivors represent up to
`r sprintf("%.3f%%", 100 * max(sim_cod_truth$checks$terminal_survivors$proportion))`
of annual abundance and
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * max(sim_cod_truth$checks$terminal_survivors$SSB_proportion))`
of annual SSB at their age-20 weight and maturity.

## Inspect fleets, surveys and the common population

```{r dashboard, eval=FALSE}
vis_tam(MultiFleet = multifleet, Aggregate = aggregate_fit, open_file = FALSE)
```

Explore the [simulated-cod dashboard](../examples/simulated-cod/index.html)
to inspect the example fits and diagnostics.

Start with each fleet under **Fisheries**. **Aggregate fishery** shows total
yield for both models and catch-at-age fits and residuals for the aggregate
model. Both models appear under **Surveys** and **Trends**.

```{r quantities}
model_order <- c("MultiFleet", "Aggregate")
ssb <- get_ssb(MultiFleet = multifleet, Aggregate = aggregate_fit)
ssb$model <- factor(ssb$model, levels = model_order)
plot_trend(ssb, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2), ylab = "SSB (tonnes)",
           add_buttons = FALSE) |>
  plotly::add_lines(data = sim_cod_truth$annual, x = ~year, y = ~SSB,
    inherit = FALSE, name = "Generating SSB",
    line = list(color = "#333333", dash = "dot"),
    hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{y} tonnes<extra>Generating SSB</extra>") |>
  add_plot_buttons()

fbar <- get_fbar(MultiFleet = multifleet, Aggregate = aggregate_fit)
fbar$model <- factor(fbar$model, levels = model_order)
fbar_truth <- with(subset(sim_cod_truth$population, age %in% 5:10),
  annual_fbar(year, F, N))
plot_trend(fbar, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2), ylab = "Average F, ages 5–10 (per year)",
           add_buttons = FALSE) |>
  plotly::add_lines(data = fbar_truth, x = ~year, y = ~F,
    inherit = FALSE, name = "Generating F",
    line = list(color = "#333333", dash = "dot"),
    hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{y} per year<extra>Generating F</extra>") |>
  add_plot_buttons()
```

The dotted lines show generating SSB and abundance-weighted F over ages
5–10. The SSB errors are percentages of generating SSB in each year.

```{r fit-errors, echo=FALSE}
comparison <- merge(ssb, sim_cod_truth$annual[c("year", "SSB")], by = "year")
stopifnot(nrow(comparison) == 2L * nrow(sim_cod_truth$annual),
  !anyDuplicated(comparison[c("model", "year")]))
comparison$relative_error <- (comparison$est - comparison$SSB) / comparison$SSB
fbar_comparison <- merge(fbar, fbar_truth, by = "year")
errors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(model_order, function(model) {
  d <- comparison[comparison$model == model, ]
  fishing <- fbar_comparison[fbar_comparison$model == model, ]
  data.frame(Model = model,
    `Mean SSB error (%)` = 100 * mean(d$relative_error),
    `Mean absolute SSB error (%)` = 100 * mean(abs(d$relative_error)),
    `Terminal SSB error (%)` = 100 * d$relative_error[which.max(d$year)],
    `Mean absolute F error (per year)` = mean(abs(fishing$est - fishing$F)),
    `Change in F, years 10 to 11` = diff(fishing$est[match(10:11, fishing$year)]),
    check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(errors, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3), row.names = FALSE)
```

Generating F changes by
`r sprintf("%+.3f", diff(fbar_truth$F[match(10:11, fbar_truth$year)]))` per year
at the trawl reduction. Differences between the fits reflect how they use
the catches and how they describe F, including the fleet model's known
timing of the trawl reduction. This example compares recovery against the
generating values because the fits use different catch observations.

```{r dashboard-export, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
dashboard_cache <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_FITS")
if (nzchar(dashboard_cache)) {
  if (!nzchar(guide_root)) stop("Set TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT to the checkout when exporting guide fits.")
  source_paths <- c(file.path("R", list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$")),
    "NAMESPACE")
  dir.create(dirname(dashboard_cache), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(models = list(MultiFleet = multifleet, Aggregate = aggregate_fit),
    inputs = sim_cod_obs, truth = sim_cod_truth,
    background = paste("### Simulated cod fisheries and surveys",
      "SimSurvey teaching data with three fleets, two regional surveys and one declining population. The trawl F target is reduced from year 11. Both fits fix M at 0.3 per year and pool ages 14 and older. MultiFleet estimates separate F by fleet. Aggregate fits an AR1 process to total F using pooled catches.",
      "### Comparison with generating values",
      paste(knitr::kable(errors, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3), row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"),
      "See the [guide](https://paulregular.github.io/tinyAM/articles/multiple-fisheries-surveys.html) for the assumptions and comparisons.",
      sep = "\n\n"),
    sources = setNames(unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(guide_root, source_paths))), source_paths),
    versions = c(tinyAM = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
      R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
      mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")))), dashboard_cache)
}
```
